name: Malchijah
overview: Malchijah was a male Levite who served as the fifth-chosen priest among the twenty-four priestly courses established for temple service. He belonged to the line of Eleazar, one of the prominent priestly families. His role highlights his important place within the organized Levitical ministry during the time of temple worship.
namesAndTitles: The name Malchijah means 'YHWH is [my] king,' reflecting a declaration of God's sovereign kingship. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 24:9, emphasizes a theocentric identity consistent with his priestly service.
familyAndRelationships: Malchijah is identified as a descendant of Eleazar, linking him to one of the primary priestly lines within the tribe of Levi. Beyond this connection, Scripture does not record additional family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Malchijah's significance lies in his role as a priest chosen to serve in one of the twenty-four courses instituted for temple worship, underscoring the organized and divinely appointed structure of Levitical ministry. Being from Eleazar's line further establishes his legitimate priestly authority. His inclusion in this list reflects the continuity of God's covenantal priesthood and the maintenance of proper worship practices in Israel.
